messages:
jamie_ts: Hey — hitting a weird one. Sample app (edge runtime) fails to bundle when installed from our pnpm monorepo. Works if I cd into packages/sdk and run the app, but when consumed via workspace it throws ModuleNotFound for '@redwood/sdk'. Anyone seen this with pnpm+exports maps + edge bundlers?

sara_devex: Yep, saw this last week. Root cause usually exports map in the package.json hiding internal paths + pnpm symlinks. Some bundlers (esbuild/rspack in edge mode) don't follow the same resolution as Node, so they fail to locate the built entry under the symlink.

anil_eng: Can you paste the package.json exports? 99% chance it's only exposing the main entry and not package.json or wildcard entries. Example problematic exports:```json
"exports": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs"}
```
This will break tools that try to reach into package subpaths or expect package.json.

jamie_ts: Here's the real snippet from @redwood/sdk:```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},"types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
Error from the edge build: `> Could not resolve "@redwood/sdk" from /workspace/apps/sample/src/main.ts`

mike_r: Quick options: (1) add a ./package.json export so bundlers can read metadata, (2) add a wildcard export ("./*": "./dist/*") so subpath imports work, or (3) publish a tiny proxy file at package root that re-exports dist for edge builds.

sara_devex: I usually do conditional exports for node vs edge when we ship both runtimes. Eg:```json
"exports": {"import": {"edge":"./dist/edge.mjs","default":"./dist/index.mjs"},"require": "./dist/index.cjs","./package.json":"./package.json"}
```
That gives bundlers a clear edge entrypoint. Also include the `./package.json` export so tools can access fields.

anil_eng: Another dev-friendly workaround in monorepos: use the workspace protocol when adding the dependency in the app so pnpm creates a proper workspace symlink resolution that some bundlers like: `pnpm add -w @redwood/sdk@workspace:. --filter "apps/sample"` — but that is a bit clunky for external devs.

jamie_ts: Types are also failing in the sample app TS server: `Could not find declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'`. We do have types in dist, but TS can't locate them when using pnpm hoisted symlinks. Any ideas?

ci-bot: build log snippet:```text
TS2307: Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk'.
Note: package.json types -> dist/index.d.ts exists in workspace package but not resolved from app root.
```

mike_r: Ensure package.json has `types` and `typesVersions` if you ship different folder layouts. Example:```json
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"typesVersions": {"*": {"@redwood/sdk": ["dist/index.d.ts"]}}
```
Also make sure the published package (or the workspace layout) actually exposes those files (pnpm sometimes prunes things if not referenced).

sara_devex: For local dev QA we added a tiny script `scripts/ensure-dist.js` that writes a root-level `index.mjs` that re-exports the dist entry. Then `postinstall` runs it in dev CI. Ugly but effective until we adjust exports. Example:```js
// scripts/ensure-dist.js
const fs = require('fs');
fs.writeFileSync('./index.mjs', `export * from './dist/index.mjs';`);
```
Add to package.json: `"postinstall": "node ./scripts/ensure-dist.js"`

anil_eng: One more important bit: edge runtimes + bundlers can use conditional exports to select smaller runtime (no node-specific crypto etc). If you don't provide an edge-specific conditional export, bundler may pick the node entry and then tree-shake things incorrectly (auth/retry hooks that patch global fetch get dropped). That causes auth token refresh to silently stop working in edge builds.

jamie_ts: Oh! We were seeing auth tokens not refreshing in samples only when run on the Vercel/Edge preview — thought it was a credentials bug. Makes sense if bundler removed side-effecting module.

mike_r: To prevent tree-shaking of important side-effect modules, mark them as side-effectful or import them explicitly in the edge entrypoint. Also consider:```json
"exports": {"import":{"edge":"./dist/edge.mjs","default":"./dist/index.mjs"},"require":"./dist/index.cjs","./package.json":"./package.json"}
```
and in `dist/edge.mjs` keep explicit `import './auth/patch-fetch.js';` at top.

jamie_ts: Thanks — that gives me a checklist: add ./package.json export, add edge conditional export, ensure types visible, or create light proxy in root. I'll try a quick PR. If anyone has a short eslint/prettier-safe script we can run in CI to detect these missing exports, ping me.

sara_devex: We should add a short devex doc + checklist for SDK packaging for monorepos (exports, types, edge conditional, postinstall fallback). I can draft one.

mike_r: +1 to doc. Also add a smoke test in the sample app CI: `pnpm --filter apps/sample build` from repo root to catch package resolution issues early. :thumbsup:

jamie_ts: Great — I'll open a tiny PR with conditional exports + package.json export and a note in the sample app readme. Thanks folks!
